Kick body: phase and summation

Each point is one rendered parameter combination. Phase compares the clean and character returns immediately before they combine. Colour shows the sum relative to the stronger individual path: red means more than 1 dB lost through cancellation. Hover a point or select a table row to inspect its settings.

Choose a point for settings and measurements.

Only windows with at least two oscillator cycles and a contributing path above −60 dB are shown. Components are projected onto the fixed octave-sub phase and its harmonics. The generator has a sub and a body at twice its frequency; 3 x sub is often just finite-window leakage and is excluded from the summary bass-loss count. The swept body is not stationary in the onset window; short-window leakage may affect the projection. The dirty high-pass protects the bass by keeping its return small there, regardless of phase. Gate-off windows are measured before the deliberate output gate. A phase angle alone does not establish cancellation: relative level matters too. These are sampled combinations, not an exhaustive proof or a prediction of a soundsystem's acoustic response.
